author: Warren
text:
Master of self rings true!

I am having a chill out night tonight, with the wife out and my Sons having friends stay over the night it leaves me downstairs with time to myself.

Your right IF, this moment does leave me feeling philosophical. It is still only early days in my journey as a whole. 5 years in a lifetime is nothing,

Hopefully i can empty my mind without talking about to many personal details and describe how trading has been a part of my life for the last 5 years. Trading itself is a small aspect of life, but impacts many areas and the adjustments you need to make along your journey are many.

Lets see what we unearth later.

author: Warren
text:
I can only tell you where i am, when you know where i have come from!

I have always been keen to better my quality of life and create choice, even from a tender age of 18 ( i think it was) I was a plumbing apprentice and had 2 greedy bosses.

Isn't it always the way it starts, you want what they have?

I set out to find anything and everything that could make me money. MLM, wholesale business and private plumbing jobs. Looking back on it now i was running round like a headless chicken. After 15 years of working for someone else, i decided to set up on my own. Bathrooms and Kitchen installing. I tell you what i was damn good at it and i grew a small business with a few employee's. But you know it was really hard, i was far too fussy to make good money.

I could see after my 80 + hour weeks, i was making no headway. It was much a case of, if you want a job doing well do it yourself. I missed the art of leveraging my time(this is important and we will come back to this another time)

This pattern continued for years, chasing the dream, i think they call it. Lets fast forward to 2007, 6 years ago

My thoughts,

There is a ceiling of productivity that i can not exceed with manual work.

If i am not in control of the situation or business, others can seal my fate eg: MLM

By this time i knew that conventional business was not for me. But i didnt really want it either. To many negative factors.

2007- the internet has me

Get rich quick being the theme................you twat Warren

information, so many opps.

See thats what you do when you are desperate like i was, i wanted to be successful more than anything. But that doesn't cut it if you dont know how to play The Game

I landed on a site where various programs were rife, It went something like this.

earn 200% on your deposit in 5 days

And strangely enough the transactions were in a digital currency. This clearly was a suckers game, but i rolled a few deposits in and paid out a few. Then the money line disappeared.

On this massive forum there was an ad for Forex, a forex trading robot. Woaw......this is different!

I really liked the sound of this a robot that would trade your money, with rights to trade only, not withdraw my funds.

COOL

After having i little look around i thought, ok i am in. i deposited 2k and set up some broker thing. Watching my broker account to see what activity there was......grhhhh

Nothing, nada.

After a few days things kicked in and it was a real nice feeling seeing this robot chug along making some money for me. Then 5 days in, an email went out "broker issue change to this other broker" oh frick sake.

New broker no action days rollin by. Some action from the robot then a malfunction. Ok this is the point where i thought stuff it

How hard can this Forex be to learn anyway

You know give a man a fish and all that!

The next 5 years are another story

But what did i learn in all the years gone by, i have a habit of pulling a positive from a negative situation.

author: mettafort
text:
A very inspiring story Warren, thank you for sharing. I thought I would share this, as its something makes sense with such a journey:

A young man once went to Socrates and asked him how he could gain wisdom. Socrates replied by asking the young man to come with him while they walked together into a nearby lake. When the water got to be about four feet deep, Socrates suddenly grabbed the young man and pushed his head under the water. Then he held it there. The young man thought it was a joke at first and did not resist. But as he was held under the water longer and longer, he became frantic. He struggled desperately to get free as his lungs burned for lack of oxygen. Finally, Socrates let him up, coughing and spluttering and gasping for air. Socrates then said, “When you desire wisdom with the same intensity that you desired to breathe, then nothing will stop you from getting it.” It’s the same with your goals

From Maximum Achievement by Brian Tracy.

Thanks again Warren,

MF

author: Warren
text:
oh man, what was i getting into....................

There i had my account, i drew out all the money from my broker, i just didnt trust anything at this point.

I opened up a demo account, ibfx was the broker with the biggest flashing ads. lol......you know you just have to.

Now i had no clue, so i had to learn how to place orders and close them, that took me a number of goes. To be really honest i didnt have a clue what i was doing.

And read the market, all i could see were candle things going up or down.

i searched for forex and one well known forum come up, there i started to look for a way ahead. many indicators and theories were tried.

I ended up like this, hmmmm.......i guess many others go through this too.

Then i found this guy that talked about naked charts and used pinbars and outside bars. Finally i could see something in the charts. coupled with this support and resistance idea, it looked pretty good. Thats where my demo account started to become a serious tool. I discovered about trends and how to add on pullbacks.

After some toying around with my demo account, i looked around for more information on how to handle an account. There was a lot of information on trading plans and risk, this is where i dug quite deep

This interested me more than profit.

First i thought in order to grow it i must first protect it. So the plan, after much jigging around was formed.

It allowed me to close out losing positions early and let good trades run.

I still use this plan today Although my entries and exit style has changed everything else is the same.

I set out from this point to manage my trades on a fresh demo account and if i could i remain profitable, even slightly in 6 months time i would go live. Well i blew a couple up, we all do, eh.

The main point was to grow the demo account, but keep the risk exposure to a minimum. So little growth was still growth.

My risk per trade was set to 2% per trade and for me to have no more than 2 trades open, unless 1 was locked in profit. then another position could be opened.

Now bear in mind, there was no race and i didnt have a ego as big as my demo account. It proves nothing, its arrogant and i have no time for it. So cross me with it at your risk.

Running a demo account, risking to large % or having 40% ish in a minus on your floating profit or loss. Yes there is captain ego over on another forum behaving just like this in order to stroke his ego.

IT HAS NO PLACE.............................IT HAS NO PLACE, i had to say it twice, because your ego in this industry will get you smashed.

letting positions run against you, not sticking to your plan and screwing with your risk, maybe great when your playing the game of DEMO. But in a LIVE account it will end up with you puking in the toilet. MARGIN CALL!

The habits your form now are the ones you carry with you, they are like baggage that are very hard to shift.

You can spend years ignoring the truth, and wonder why 8 years down the line you cant make this work. You know the honest answer, its because while you were dicking around, the only person you cheated was yourself.

I was using confluence of pinbars and outside bars at trendlines and stacking orders on pullbacks. support and resistance played a key part too, but failed and i couldnt understand one thing.

If i had a previous high and price was slightly falling short on the next visit, then dropping hard, why was this. It left a unsolved puzzle in my mind.

My demo account after 6 months was nicely in the green, i felt ready to take the next step and go live. I loaded a small amount and proceeded to work as i had done previously. Following my plan and keeping my risk low, this made logical sense to me.

It was backed up by going on FF and watching people throw money away by having no clue and going at it hap hazzard. There i met a crazy northern guy, he was mocking the "know all, know nothing " bunch. It seemed to make sense what he was showing. I do hunt information out when i feel its going to be good, so i found his thread.

It was Redsword, i must have read through his thread twice over the next few days, i felt i had found the missing part of the puzzle.

yawnnnnnn..................late here, carry on with the interesting stuff tomorow

author: Warren
text:
Just another stage in the journey.......................

After a number of chats with Red, some things began to click. When i looked at the charts i focused and tried to look for poles, looking at the base of the pole where the source is. Then i could see a return to the base of the pole (the source).

I could see this supply and demand on the chart. But i couldnt really trade it. I just didnt see why some zones held and others not.

Now i had been looking at charts for a few years by this point and i trained my eye to pick up the areas of interest first and work from there. The more you do something,your brain becomes accustomed to recognizing to filtering out what it doesn't need, or it feels it doesn't.

Your mind is a sorting machine, you want to retain good information and disregard misinformation, this will take time.

How much time will depend on you, usually the time it takes to rewire your brain occurs as you experience positive and negative effects. But it depends on how you address them.

Accept that you will always have losing trades, it is how many you have and what risk exposure your account has in the market.

That is something i have always thought that needs to take first place. So my account has always had a number of small loses and a number of bigger wins. My account could go a few days with not much positive activity and then a nice trade would come off and blow away the small loss.

You will find that your account growth will always move in surges and lulls. But when you look at it over time it is constantly building. Do not be disheartened at this. And also do not alter from your trading plan in order to get quick fix trades.

After sometime with Red i was using a combination of the old s/r, trendlines and pa. And looking at poles, up to supply or down to demand. My focus was on a return to the source or base of pole. At times this worked well, as we now know it is only part of the story.

From the moment you start trading you begin to find out the type of person you are and where your weaknesses cause you problems. This is vital that you embrace this as you develop.

I can not scalp to save my life, i spent 6 months full time where i had daily swings going and scalped during the day also. My scalping side was really break even. Where my swings were just as the have been for a long time profitable.

Does this mean i cant trade?

NO, of course not, it just means i am more suited or wired for longer tf.

So, if i had learnt and stayed a scalper i would have probably given up by now.

The question that can decide your fate is "What type of trader are you?"

There are a thousand ways to skin this cat, what is your way?

Trading is about self discovery, you learn heaps about the type of person you are and this spills out into other areas of your life. Trading or any other activity in your life is a working part, If it runs badly, it effects other parts.

Think of it like a car, all parts must work in order to have a whole working vehicle. Something important packs up and nothing else can be utilized.

It is a known fact that the average working class person spends more time planning their next holiday than they do planning their financial future.

There is a difference between "The Have and the Have nots". Its all in the mindset,you keep thinking and doing things like a poor person and thats all you will ever be. Or you can think like a rich person does and you can start to do as they do.

Give 5k to a average working class person and they think "what can i spend it on"

Give 5k to a rich person and they will think "What can i invest it on"

This was the biggest hurdle for me, watching my account grow from 3 to 4 to 5 figures and more, it gets harder to keep your hands off it and let it grow. I had a figure in mind where i wanted to get to, which i reevaluated every year. Why?, its what rich people do, they monitor everything.

Where have i come from?

Where am i now?

Where am i going to?

You see when you make it past demo, it opens up another set of issues LIVE account trading and the games it plays on our mind. But once we are successfully building our account, after sometime things can start getting serious.

What goals are you working towards?

are they material or financial, Family or relationship based. Moving home or moving country. How will this money impact your life? How will it change and shape your future.?

All these things need planning.

What are you going to do about tax and paying what is due?

Will you start a ltd company or a trust?, with these surplus funds will you venture into property or start some kind of business? How will you keep the tax you are liable to pay to a minimum?

How will you protect what you have?

Spread the money between different brokers, spread money in different bank accounts.

If you have made excessive amounts and you have broker accounts, property, precious metals,art, businesses.

How much of a percentage will you keep as liquid cash? and will the % value need to change from time to time.

Will your success change the social circles you move in? Will people change their view of you? be it positive or negative, it will happen.

Will you tell everyone openly about your spoils and worth? or keep it quiet and just keep yourself to yourself?

When you have money and it shows, the % of people trying to extract that money from you will grow, as they use legal or illegal methods to acquire it from you. Be assured, they will.

How does this money effect your partner and your children? What happens when you die?

Best make sure these things are in place ahead of time, you will now when they are needed.

I asked myself these questions years ago, they made logical sense at the time. I have be implementing and reviewing ever since.

Do i know where i am going next? Sure i do

Am i prepared for it? Absolutely

author: coast2coast
text:
I'm pretty new here but I think this is my favourite thread so far!

What stands out to me is that your style seems incredibly similar to mine which is always encouraging. It's easy to see what other people are doing and allow it to sway your thinking so whilst all of my success comes on higher timeframes and picking the coast to coast moves like you've described here, I see some of these charts people post where they seem to have taken every swing to the pip on a 5min chart or whatever it might be and it can make you feel very inferior!

Knowing yourself is such a key thing and I've learnt that for me, if I try to scalp/day trade I end up messing about with the order too much, I do far better taking trades on the hourly and above and then just leaving them and treating it as mechanically as possible. The other key is I use tight stops and try to enter as close to the zones as possible so if it does break the zone I'm trading from I'm out straight away. It means plenty of losses, (around 30-40% of my trades are losses) but my winning trades are always far bigger than the losses.

I would sum up my approach as purely statistical. I don't worry about whether any individual trade is a winner or a loser, the only thing I care about is whether I feel the trade I've entered has given me a statstical edge. The key factor for myself in the journey to becoming consistently profitable was getting to grips with the mental approach, not the technical approach (although that's of course hugely important as well). Learning to let my trades run to their targets was the key and the only way I could do that was to detatch myself from the individual trade results and look at the bigger picture, again that's pretty much what you've explained earlier on.

Anyway sorry to bombard your thread with this essay! I was just really chuffed to see your trading and your mindset was so similar in style to mine, very encouraging!

I do not give a hoot as long as its in my plan. I feel that is what gets me by. Once i make a decision, its final.

I cant be right all the time, but i am right enough, for me.
